name: Jingqianshu granules (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Placebo-controlled trial, 156 women with premenstrual syndrome (by mouth, 3 cycles): adverse events mild and similar (4.81% vs 3.92% on placebo), none serious. Herbs not listed.
text: Jingqianshu granules are a Chinese patented herbal medicine taken by mouth; the cited trial abstract does not list the herbs. In a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 156 women with premenstrual syndrome were assigned 2:1 to the granules (104) or placebo (52) for three menstrual cycles, followed by three cycles of follow-up, and safety was assessed by adverse-event reporting and laboratory monitoring. Adverse events were mild and similar in the two groups (4.81% with the granules, 3.92% with placebo), and no serious events were reported; the abstract does not say what the adverse events were or give the laboratory results. This is the only human safety source found in PubMed searches under the formula's names, and it does not report safety beyond the treatment and follow-up cycles. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
